video.title: IT'S NOT OVER UNTIL YOU WIN - Georgia Dome (Les Brown's Greatest Hits)

motivational.video_read: This is Les Brown's full classic 'It's not over until you win' convention speech: thirty minutes of personal-humiliation stories (labelled educable mentally retarded, sleeping in his office, people laughing at him) converted into vows and call-and-response affirmations. The material lives everywhere in it — the Connect Four story, the Mr. Washington thread, the Penobscot Building story — and it is the densest stretch of publishable moments I have read in this category.

near_misses.why_not: The reframe that dreams are given to us for the purpose of accomplishing them is genuinely interesting, but the sentence arrives convoluted and depends on the 'think about your dream' framing before it; unsure it completes for a cold stranger.
The shoeshine creativity anecdote is charming but the takeaway is sales craft — amaze your customers — aimed at the convention audience; nothing shifts in how the 2am viewer sees themselves.
A call-and-response recap of affirmations; it summarises the speech rather than delivering a landing of its own.
Goal-writing and planning walkthrough — correct and administrative, no charge, changes nothing about who the viewer is.

The 'if you know the why, you can endure almost any how' line is quotable but arrives garbled ('less nietzsche said') and folded into the mother-home anecdote, so it does not cut out cleanly on its own.

skipped.what: opening address and 'think about your dream' framing
dream, risk-takers and biography of humble beginnings — setup, not a landing
fear of failure/comfort/worthiness list plus his résumé of achievements (book, specials, talk show)
customer-service and integrity advice aimed at the distributor audience
continuation of the hard-times story past the envelope payoff
'you're the one' repetition and tape-listening setup
buying his mother a home and the birth-mother adoption story — moving, but it lands as emotion without a turn for the viewer until L0234
closing recaps, handshakes and the hungry chant

clips.title: If you want a thing bad enough — you'll get it
